strategy.summary: GET /products filters the in-memory catalogue by a case-insensitive name substring `q`, pages with `limit` (default 20, capped at MAX_LIMIT) and `offset`, returns { total, items }, and refuses non-whole limit/offset or limit < 1 with 400. Integration tests start the real http server in-process (as the existing test does) and assert on responses.
outOfScope: GET /products/:id and POST /orders (not part of this ticket)
the search box UI (not in this repository)
assumptions: The code's cap (MAX_LIMIT = 50 in src/app.js) is right, not the README's 'up to 100' (asked as Q1); tests import MAX_LIMIT and DEFAULT_LIMIT rather than hard-coding them.

The catalogue is the fixed in-memory PRODUCTS list from src/catalogue.js (120 products, 15 per name); tests import PRODUCTS for the full count and rely on its names for search data. No service is faked: the real app runs in-process on an OS-chosen port.
Results are ordered by id (catalogue order), as the README says.
An empty `limit=` or `offset=` counts as not a whole number and is refused with 400, as the code does.
openQuestions: README says limit goes up to 100, code caps at 50 (Q1).

acceptanceCriteria.text: q matches products whose name contains it, case-insensitively; without q every product is listed.
Results are paged with limit and offset, the response includes the total number of matches, and limits above the maximum are capped.
A limit or offset that isn't a whole number, or a limit below 1, is refused with 400.

review.standard: Teardown runs on every exit / setup and teardown helpers fail with the cause, never use an unchecked result
review.summary: startServer never rejects: listen() errors are not listened for and close() resolves with its error argument instead of rejecting, so a setup or teardown failure is hidden or turned into a generic timeout.
review.failureScenario: If listen emits 'error' (e.g. EMFILE/EACCES on a constrained CI host), the promise on line 6 never settles and beforeAll fails only with Vitest's generic 10s hook timeout, not the real error; afterAll then throws a TypeError on `server.close` because `server` is undefined (test/products-search.test.js:13, test/products.test.js:12), adding noise. On teardown, `server.close(resolve)` passes any error (e.g. ERR_SERVER_NOT_RUNNING) to resolve, so a failed close counts as a clean teardown. Suggested fix: `new Promise((resolve, reject) => { server.once('error', reject); server.listen(0, resolve); })` and `close: () => new Promise((resolve, reject) => server.close((err) => (err ? reject(err) : resolve())))`, with `afterAll(() => server?.close())`.

review.standard: Vitest: use it.each with a $property/%s title so each case reports a distinct, readable name
review.summary: The parameterised limit and offset 400 cases have titles with no placeholder, so every row reports the same name and a failure doesn't say which value was accepted.
review.failureScenario: If the app started accepting limit=1e2, the report shows 'refuses a limit that is not a whole number with 400' failing with no mention of 1e2 among the five identical titles; the same goes for the offset table at line 73. Adding a placeholder such as 'refuses limit=%j with 400' fixes it.

questions.question: The README says `limit` goes "up to 100", but the code caps it at 50 (MAX_LIMIT in src/app.js). Which cap is intended?
questions.assumption: The code is right: tests import MAX_LIMIT (50) from src/app.js and assert a large limit returns exactly MAX_LIMIT items; the README mismatch is listed as a follow-up.
questions.answer: The cap is 50, as the code does. The README is out of date; leave it as it is and test against 50.
